27.note: This project has enough surviving documentation to support a fuller case study. The sections below describe documented responsibilities, technologies and visible interface behavior; they do not claim formal user research that is not recorded.

ux.title: Responsive conference information with a dynamic agenda
ux.intro: The strongest interface evidence in the surviving TCT 2014 material is the way a large conference information set was organized across desktop, tablet and mobile, including a dynamic agenda rather than a static schedule.

panels.title: Information structure
panels.copy: Conference content, schedules and industry information had to remain understandable across multiple related web experiences. The documented work includes TCT and TCT Industry interfaces, responsive layouts and agenda views.

panels.title: Interaction + data
panels.copy: The dynamic agenda used interactive transitions and asynchronously loaded content connected to the same data source used by the conference app, giving the website and app a shared information foundation.

5.note: This project supports a full design-system/campaign case study because the surviving portfolio documents the identity across print, email, web graphics, production and fulfillment.

ux.title: One event identity across many user touchpoints
ux.intro: The design problem was larger than a single invitation. Guests encountered event information through invitation components, response materials, hotel and directions information, email and supporting event pieces.

panels.title: Information hierarchy
panels.copy: The invitation, RSVP, dinner selection, hotel information and directions each carried different information while remaining visibly part of the same event package.

panels.title: System consistency
panels.copy: The Gatsby-inspired identity was extended across print, email, website graphics, sponsorship and event materials instead of redesigning every touchpoint independently.
